title: SPROUT: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Software Engineering
data_curation: RL training uses SWE-bench Rebench v2 Filtered, from which the top 2,115 tasks ranked by golden-patch length are selected to emphasize long-horizon work. Reward is the task verifier's binary terminal reward R in {0,1} (test suite), plus diagnostic feedback d (failing tests, final patch, verifier output) that is used only by the analyst/reviewer roles and never shown to the learner. Rollout-collection experiments use the 113-task public DeepSWE, 89-task Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 51-task SWE-bench Pro v2 Hard. Guided starting turns written during FF repair are filtered by a judge that rejects turns mentioning checkpoints, other branches or hidden tests.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is a single full-parameter RL stage on Qwen3.8-27B with no SFT or preference stage; instead, each task's group is built adaptively from root outcomes (TT/TF: unguided children from a reviewer-chosen boundary; FF: verifier-guided repair children). Configuration: 32 prompts per update x 8 rollouts (256-rollout nominal batch), 128K max context, temperature 1.0, thinking enabled at xhigh effort, Adam at constant LR 2e-6, KL coefficient 0, on 8x B300 with TP=2, CP=4 and a 32,768-token per-GPU microbatch cap.
method: SPROUT (SnaPshot-based RollOUT) lets rollouts resume and branch from any intermediate turn boundary. (1) Restorable execution: each attempt runs in a Firecracker-style microVM; after every assistant turn the VM disk delta is saved as an incremental block-level OverlayBD layer paired with the agent context; synchronous shell calls with no background processes mean guest memory never needs capture, and branches get isolated copy-on-write layers. (2) Verifier-guided backtracking: the same actor, under analyst and reviewer role prompts, reads failures plus verifier diagnostics, picks parent attempt and boundary, and writes a starting turn in the actor's own voice (reasoning + bash calls) rather than a user hint; collection uses R=2 rounds with K1=4 and K2=3 branches. (3) Training: each task gets 2 roots x 3 children = 8 attempts; FF children get advantage A=R (successes +1, failures 0), other groups use GRPO-normalized advantages; token masks drop shared prefixes and observations; PPO-clip surrogate with no KL, trained without the review context so it distills guided behavior into the actor. A scan-free relaxed state projection matches reusable states with 100% precision at 0.201 ms.
eval_metrics: Rollout collection: resolve rate, normalized recovery rate (R_method - R_Pass@1)/(1 - R_Pass@1), total execution steps and tokens, against Pass@1/Pass@4 (four fresh attempts), entropy-based branching and Shepherd, on DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Pro v2 Hard using Kimi K3, Qwen3.8-27B, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Luna. On DeepSWE, SPROUT reaches 98.2% (Kimi K3, vs 92.0 Pass@4), 85.8% (GPT-5.6 Luna, vs 68.1) and 78.6% (Qwen3.8-27B, vs 71.7) with 47.9-67.7% fewer tokens. RL evaluation reports success rates on the three benchmarks plus wall-clock time per training step. Ablations (GPT-5.6 Luna, DeepSWE): no injected starting turn drops resolve from 85.8 to 49.6; reward-only review drops it to 53.1.
key_results: RL on Qwen3.8-27B with SPROUT reaches 84.3 / 40.7 / 64.0 on SWE-bench Pro v2 Hard / DeepSWE / Terminal-Bench 2.1, beating basic GRPO (74.5 / 33.6 / 39.3) by 13.9 points on average while cutting time per step from 3.77 h to 2.28 h (-39.5%). As a sampler it beats Pass@4 on every model, by up to 23.6 points (Qwen3.8-27B on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 66.3 to 89.9), using 32-52% of Pass@4's tokens.
evolution_note: SPROUT extends GRPO-style RLVR for SWE agents (in the line of SWE-RL and DeepSWE-style training) by addressing the all-fail-group problem on long horizons, where zero-advantage groups waste hours-long rollouts. It reacts to branching RL methods (VinePPO, TreeRL, CBPO, BPO, Shepherd) that branch only within the conversation, snapshot only a few container states, or delegate branch choice to a stronger model. Full-filesystem per-turn microVM checkpoints plus self-guided, verifier-informed repair make branching practical for tasks with hundreds of tool calls, and its depth-vs-breadth study suggests sequential review rounds are more token-efficient than wider parallel sampling.
